_comment: A component-structured codebase, deliberately unlike static-page's single hand-written HTML file. Two reasons it exists: markup lives in .tsx across several files so a finding has to pick between components, and the contrast violation's cause is in a stylesheet while the element is in markup - which is the case the markup-first tiebreak must NOT win, since the real evidence is in the CSS.

violations.description: Ensure contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG thresholds
violations.help: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds

finding.title: color-contrast
finding.detail: The 'Get started' button's label is near-invisible against its background.

expected.rationale: The colours are declared in .btn--primary, so the stylesheet is where a developer fixes this - the markup only names the class. Deliberately a case the deterministic search is NOT expected to get on its own: Hero.tsx matches more anchors (it has the class and the label text) and legitimately outranks the CSS. Both files reach the candidates, which is the search's job; choosing between them needs to know that colour lives in CSS, which is judgment and therefore the LLM's job. So --search-only is expected to fail this one and the full run is expected to pass it - the gap between the two modes on this case is the measurement worth having.

finding.title: Primary CTA reads 'Get started' instead of 'Start free trial'
finding.detail: The hero's primary button is labelled 'Get started' in production; the design shows 'Start free trial'.

expected.rationale: The anchor and its label text in Hero.tsx. Must not land in Footer.tsx, which also contains a link with a class starting 'footer__link' - a different component entirely.

finding.title: Footer is missing the newsletter signup
finding.detail: The design shows an email capture form in the footer. Production shows only a privacy link.

expected.rationale: There is no newsletter markup anywhere in this checkout, so no_match is correct. Pairs with the static-page no_match case: two codebases of different shapes both have to know when to stop.
